guide.title: Prefixes change meaning
guide.rule: self- often concerns the person; well- often describes a positive standard. Learn the complete combination rather than attaching either prefix to any adjective.
guide.example: She is well informed about current affairs.

guide.title: Describe change precisely
guide.rule: Use slight for a small degree and dramatic for a large noticeable change. Time idioms have whole-phrase meanings.
guide.example: The organisers amended the timetable in good time.

guide.title: Meaning in a social context
guide.rule: Distinguish a community, its norms and the pressure to conform. A description of one group is not a rule about everyone.
guide.example: The community welcomes people from different backgrounds.

guide.title: Words for scientific discussion
guide.rule: Separate noun and adjective forms such as chemistry, chemist and chemical. Natural describes origin and does not itself establish safety.
guide.example: The label explains the chemical reaction.

guide.title: Academic word families
guide.rule: Learn related forms such as hypothesis / hypothetical and commit / commitment together with their sentence patterns.
guide.example: The students made a concerted effort.

guide.title: Choose a precise description
guide.rule: A jingle is a tune, a slogan a phrase and a billboard a large physical display. Persuasion words differ in strength and context.
guide.example: The company uses a catchy slogan.

guide.title: Description and evaluation
guide.rule: Travel adjectives can overlap. State whether you mean remoteness, comfort, appearance or memorable experience.
guide.example: The village offers basic accommodation.

guide.title: Public institutions and prefixes
guide.rule: Learn institutional vocabulary in context. The prefix mis- often signals an action performed wrongly.
guide.example: Residents discussed the local council proposal.

guide.title: Species, groups and habitats
guide.rule: Learn animal group nouns with their usual animals. Distinguish a predator from its prey and a habitat from a shelter.
guide.example: The project aims to protect the habitat.

guide.title: Processes and word families
guide.rule: Learn process verbs with noun forms such as evaporate / evaporation. Astronomical can mean extremely large when describing a cost.
guide.example: The liquid changes through evaporation.

guide.title: Materials and movement
guide.rule: Rotate refers to turning about an axis. When revolve has an orbital meaning, specify what the object moves around.
guide.example: The students kept a log of their designs.

guide.title: Trends and resources
guide.rule: A passing trend is short-lived. Distinguish preserving something, retaining it and discarding it in context.
guide.example: Some people follow every passing trend.

guide.title: Urban collocations
guide.rule: Learn urban sprawl, traffic congestion and employment opportunities as complete combinations. Rural living has varied advantages and disadvantages.
guide.example: Traffic congestion increased near the station.

guide.title: Problems and responses
guide.rule: Aggravate and exacerbate make a problem worse. Alleviate and mitigate reduce its severity; rectify puts an error right.
guide.example: We need to identify the underlying problem.

guide.title: Literal and idiomatic weather
guide.rule: Drought is lack of rain. In weather the storm, the storm represents a difficult period rather than necessarily literal weather.
guide.example: The farmers sow seeds in the spring.

guide.title: Energy words and forms
guide.rule: Renewable, recyclable and rechargeable describe different properties. Learn emit with emissions and consume with consumption.
guide.example: The turbines harness the power of the wind.

guide.title: Business combinations
guide.rule: Say draw up a contract, meet a deadline and be in charge of. One employee is a member of staff.
guide.example: The manager will chair the meeting.

guide.title: Acts, people and patterns
guide.rule: Crime names the act or category; criminal can name a person or modify a noun. Learn accuse of and arrest for.
guide.example: The discussion focused on crime prevention.

guide.title: Evidence and perspective
guide.rule: Separate an attributed opinion from a supported fact. Biased and impartial describe different approaches to reporting.
guide.example: The report should distinguish facts from opinions.

guide.title: Experience and cause
guide.rule: Terrified describes the person feeling fear; terrifying describes its cause. Opinions about art often depend on taste.
guide.example: The actors rehearsed the play before opening night.

title: Learning vocabulary
test: Dictionaries, word families and learning records

guide.title: Record a useful sense
guide.rule: Include part of speech, meaning, usage, register and an example. One translation rarely covers every meaning.
guide.example: An example sentence places a word in context.

title: IELTS Reading
test: Main ideas, details, evidence and question types

guide.title: Evidence decides the response
guide.rule: False contradicts a statement; Not Given means the passage does not settle it. Choose headings for main ideas rather than isolated words.
guide.example: The heading expresses the main idea.

title: IELTS Writing
test: Data, comparisons, cohesion and accurate wording

guide.title: Report what data shows
guide.rule: Use number with countable nouns and amount with uncountable nouns. Distinguish a rise by a change from a rise to a final value.
guide.example: The number of visitors increased steadily.

guide.title: Listen for meaning and corrections
guide.rule: Predict the needed information from headings, then use the speaker’s final corrected details and the sense that fits the context.
guide.example: The speaker corrected the spelling of the address.

title: IELTS Speaking
test: Developing, linking and paraphrasing spoken ideas

guide.title: Develop rather than list
guide.rule: Answer directly, support the idea and link it clearly. Paraphrase unknown expressions. Personal rehearsal here has no automatic band score.
guide.example: A relevant example can develop an answer.
